# PROPRIETARY INFORMATION AND INVENTIONS ASSIGNMENT (PIIA) CLAUSE
### (Master Boilerplate Clause for Employment, Independent Contractor, and Advisory Agreements)

---

### SECTION [__]. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION AND INVENTIONS ASSIGNMENT

**(a) Definition of Inventions and Works.**  
As used herein, "**Inventions**" shall mean all inventions, original works of authorship, developments, concepts, improvements, designs, discoveries, algorithms, source code, object code, software architectures, database schemas, scripts, data models, state management logic, application programming interfaces (APIs), workflows, formulas, processes, techniques, know-how, trade secrets, documentation, instructional frameworks (including OptimumPrimers™ curriculum and STAR behavioral interview modules), and CalAIM/Medi-Cal H0038 billing translation engines, whether or not patentable, copyrightable, or protectable as trade secrets, that are conceived, developed, authored, created, reduced to practice, or learned by the Employee/Contractor ("**Service Provider**"), either alone or jointly with others:
1. during the term of Service Provider’s engagement or employment with **Peer Notebook LLC**, a California limited liability company (the "**Company**"); and
2. which (i) relate in any manner to the actual or demonstrably anticipated business, research, development, products, software, or services of the Company (specifically including, but not limited to, the "Peer Notebook" software application, peernotebook.com, offline-first clinical documentation systems, peer support workflows, and health plan billing systems); or (ii) result from, are derived from, or are suggested by any work performed by Service Provider for the Company; or (iii) are developed using any Company equipment, supplies, facilities, servers, repositories, trade secrets, or confidential information.

**(b) Work Made for Hire.**  
Service Provider acknowledges and agrees that all copyrightable works, software programs, scripts, modules, documentation, text, designs, graphics, and instructional materials authored, created, or prepared by Service Provider within the scope of Service Provider’s engagement with the Company are and shall be deemed a **"work made for hire"** as defined in Section 101 of the United States Copyright Act (17 U.S.C. § 101) for the sole and exclusive benefit of the Company.

**(c) Absolute, Global, and Perpetual Assignment.**  
To the fullest extent that any Invention, work of authorship, patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property right does not qualify as a "work made for hire" under applicable law, or to the extent that legal title to any such Invention does not immediately vest exclusively in the Company by operation of law, Service Provider hereby **irrevocably, unconditionally, globally, and perpetually assigns, transfers, conveys, and sets over unto the Company (Peer Notebook LLC)**, and its successors and assigns, all of Service Provider’s right, title, and interest throughout the universe in and to:
1. any and all Inventions;
2. any and all domestic and international patents, patent applications, utility models, and statutory invention registrations relating thereto;
3. any and all copyrights, copyright registrations, moral rights, rental rights, and renewal rights;
4. any and all trade secrets, know-how, and proprietary technical processes; and
5. all causes of action, claims, demands, and rights of recovery for past, present, and future infringement, misappropriation, or violation of any of the foregoing rights.

This assignment is effective automatically upon the conception, creation, development, or reduction to practice of each such Invention, without the requirement of any further consideration or execution of additional documents.

**(d) California Labor Code Section 2870 Notice.**  
In accordance with California Labor Code Section 2870, Service Provider is hereby advised that the assignment provisions of this Section shall not apply to an Invention that qualifies fully under California Labor Code Section 2870(a), which provides:
> *"Any provision in an employment agreement which provides that an employee shall assign, or offer to assign, any of his or her rights in an invention to his or her employer shall not apply to an invention that the employee developed entirely on his or her own time without using the employer’s equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information except for those inventions that either: (1) Relate at the time of conception or reduction to practice of the invention to the employer’s business, or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development of the employer; or (2) Result from any work performed by the employee for the employer."*

Service Provider bears the burden of establishing that an Invention qualifies for exemption under California Labor Code Section 2870.

**(e) Waiver of Moral Rights.**  
To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Service Provider hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives, releases, and quits claims to any and all "moral rights," rights of paternity, rights of integrity, rights of attribution, and similar rights that Service Provider may have in any jurisdiction worldwide with respect to any Invention or work created for or assigned to the Company.

**(f) Power of Attorney and Further Assurances.**  
Service Provider agrees to assist the Company (at the Company's expense) in every proper way to secure, register, protect, and enforce the Company’s rights in the Inventions and intellectual property in all countries, including executing all formal assignment documents, patent applications, copyright registration forms (such as USCO Form TX), declarations, and affidavits. If the Company is unable for any reason to secure Service Provider’s signature on any document needed to apply for, prosecute, or enforce any patent, copyright, or trademark registration, Service Provider hereby **irrevocably designates and appoints the Company and its duly authorized officers and agents as Service Provider’s agent and attorney-in-fact**, coupled with an interest, to act for and on Service Provider’s behalf to execute, verify, and file any such applications and instruments with the USPTO, U.S. Copyright Office, or international registry.
